restore.title: Restore
restore.caption: Bring a JSON export back in — into this login, as new accounts.
restore.body: Every trading account in the file becomes a new account, labelled “(restored)”. Nothing you already have is changed or merged: tags and playbooks with the same name are reused, and journal days you have already written are left alone. P&L, pips and R are recomputed rather than copied.

restore.createdJournal: {count, plural, one {# journal day} other {# journal days}}
restore.createdTags: {count, plural, one {# new tag} other {# new tags}}
restore.createdPlaybooks: {count, plural, one {# new playbook} other {# new playbooks}}
restore.createdAttachments: {count, plural, one {# attachment link} other {# attachment links}}
restore.skippedBacktest: {count, plural, one {# backtest account} other {# backtest accounts}} — backtest runs and their settings aren't in the export, so the trades would have no run to belong to.
restore.skippedUnknownSymbols: {count, plural, one {# trade} other {# trades}} on symbols this instance doesn't have ({symbols}). Ask the owner to add them under Instruments, then restore again.
restore.skippedInvalidTrades: {count, plural, one {# trade} other {# trades}} whose fills don't add up (an exit before any entry, or more closed than opened).
restore.skippedJournal: {count, plural, one {# journal day} other {# journal days}} you already have an entry for — yours was kept.
restore.skippedUploads: {count, plural, one {# uploaded attachment} other {# uploaded attachments}} — the export holds only a pointer to the file, not the file itself.
restore.skippedLinks: {count, plural, one {# attachment link} other {# attachment links}} that aren't https.

restore.skippedAliases: {count, plural, one {# symbol mapping} other {# symbol mappings}} you already have, or for symbols this instance doesn't know.
